requirements.text: Stuff the paper into the cup.
requirements.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup

outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: Can the edited object be identified as the source paper, and does comparison with the source show any observable movement toward putting it into the source cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if source-paper identity is supported and visible evidence shows the paper has begun entering the source cup. Fail only if the relevant objects are identifiable and visible evidence establishes no movement toward putting the paper into the cup. Unknown if paper or cup identity, visibility, or movement cannot be determined. Proximity alone is not progress.
nodes.binding: Assess the requested paper-into-cup edit by comparing source and edited images. Do not assume the printed card is the source paper or the reddish round object is the source cup; ground identity and movement in visible evidence.

nodes.question: Given the source-grounded object identities, is the paper visibly inside the cup, and is there evidence it is stuffed into it rather than merely touching or resting on the rim?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the source paper is visibly inside the source cup and evidence supports that it is stuffed into it. Fail only when identities and visibility are clear and the paper is not inside or stuffed into the cup. Unknown when identity, visibility, or placement is ambiguous. Mere proximity or rim contact is insufficient.
nodes.binding: Use the source image and edited image to ground paper and cup identity; use the ancestor observation as context but inspect the placement proposition independently. Do not assume the edited card or round object matches the source objects.

nodes.question: With the source paper and source cup identified, does visible evidence show the paper entering the cup, and does it establish stuffing rather than only initial entry?
nodes.criteria: Pass if visible evidence establishes the paper is stuffed into the identified cup. Fail if identities and visibility are clear and the paper has not entered the cup. Unknown if identity, visibility, or extent of entry cannot be determined. Entry without evidence of stuffing is not a pass for completion.
nodes.binding: Inspect the source and edited images, using ancestor observations as context. Assess the extent of the requested paper-into-cup action; do not infer stuffing from proximity, contact, or an ambiguous object match.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Complete only when s2 and entry_extent establish stuffing into the identified source cup. Partial only when s1 or entry_extent evidences progress but completion is not established. Absent only when evidence establishes no requested progress. If identity, visibility, or necessary extent evidence is unresolved, report unknown; do not convert uncertainty or mere non-completion into absence.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The fulfillment rule is contradictory and can misclassify incomplete progress. It says partial when s1 or entry_extent evidences progress, but entry_extent can pass only when stuffing is established, which s2 also requires for complete; thus a pass on entry_extent cannot coherently mean incomplete progress. Conversely, s1 can fail for no movement while entry_extent is unknown, leaving the readout without a clear composition rule for known negative evidence plus unresolved extent. The support checks also overlap: s2 and entry_extent both assess whether the paper is stuffed into the cup, rather than separating placement from action extent. This does not provide a clean, non-overlapping composition of progress, completion, and uncertainty."}
